record.paper_title: SOME OPEN QUESTIONS ON ARITHMETIC ZARISKI PAIRS
record.context_brief: Non-equivalence of braid monodromies for other projected Eyral–Oka pairs
record.original_question: For the additional candidate arithmetic Zariski pairs obtained from the Eyral–Oka curves by projecting from the singular points of type E6 or A2, can one prove that the resulting braid monodromy factorizations are not equivalent, thereby distinguishing those pairs topologically?

evidence.quote: Eyral-Oka curves give rise to other arithmetic Zariski pairs, namely using the projections from the singular points of type E6 and A2. When projecting from a point of type E6 it does not matter which one because of the symmetry of the curves which exchanges both points. One can compute the braid monodromy factorizations using again the fact that they are strongly real curves. In these cases, it is more involved to prove that the braid monodromy factorizations are not equivalent. In a future work we will use the computed representations to distinguish the braid monodromies using diagonal representations.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the Eyral–Oka sextic curves: a Galois-conjugate pair of complex projective plane curves of degree 6 defined over a number field, sharing the same combinatorial type of singularities (in particular containing two singular points of type E6 and singular points of type A2). For each curve in the pair, one may choose a projection from a smooth point onto a generic line and obtain a braid monodromy factorization in the braid group of the corresponding fiber; equivalence of two such factorizations is generated by Hurwitz moves and global conjugation, and equivalence is a topological invariant of the embedded curve.

Beyond the classical projection from a generic smooth point, one obtains further candidate arithmetic Zariski pairs by projecting from the singular points of the curves: 
(i) projection from a singular point of type E6 (the symmetry exchanging the two E6 points makes the choice immaterial), and 
(ii) projection from a singular point of type A2.

In each of cases (i) and (ii), the two curves are strongly real, so their braid monodromy factorizations can be computed explicitly. 

Prove that in each of these two cases the resulting braid monodromy factorizations of the conjugate curves are not equivalent (under Hurwitz equivalence and global conjugation), thereby establishing that the pairs of curves obtained via these projections form genuine (topologically non-equivalent) arithmetic Zariski pairs.

artifact.status_search_result: A web search returned related literature on arithmetic Zariski pairs, Eyral–Oka curves, and braid monodromy factorizations, but did not produce a clear, recent paper announcing a proof that the braid monodromy factorizations from the E6 and A2 projections of the Eyral–Oka curves are inequivalent. The original announcement indicated that diagonal representations would be used in future work to distinguish them, but no definitive resolution was located in the search.
